question: Which of the following is the temperature range in a clinical thermometer?
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

The correct temperature range for a clinical thermometer is **35°C to 42°C**. This range is specifically chosen to cover the normal body temperature of a healthy human (around 37°C) and possible variations due to fever or hypothermia. Temperatures below or above this range are not typically associated with human body temperature and, therefore, are outside the scope of a clinical thermometer.

 
• Normal human body temperature ranges from 36.1°C to 37.2°C (97°F to 99°F).
 
• Fever is typically indicated when body temperature exceeds 37.5°C (99.5°F), which falls within this range.
 
• Hypothermia, which occurs when body temperature drops below 35°C (95°F), is rare and usually requires specialized equipment for measurement.
 
• This range allows the thermometer to be sensitive and precise for small variations in body temperature, which are critical for medical diagnosis.

The clinical thermometer is typically marked with this range and includes a constriction in the capillary tube to hold the mercury (or other indicating fluid) at the measured temperature until it is manually reset. This feature allows for accurate readings and easy observation.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 2:** 35°C to 42°C

This option correctly identifies the standard temperature range of a clinical thermometer. It encompasses the normal and febrile temperature ranges of the human body, making it suitable for medical use
